title: New-Account Period, Deposited Check Availability and Check Writing on Personal Checking
content:
New-account treatment on a Personal Checking account runs for the number of calendar days after the opening date that the tier sets. While it runs, a deposited check posts and becomes available on the business day after deposit that the tier names rather than on the next business day. Separately, each tier states whether paper checks can be written on the account at all.

| Tier | Length of the new-account period (calendar days after opening) | Business day after deposit on which a check posts while that period runs | Paper checks can be written on the account |
|---|---|---|---|
| Access Checking | 30 | 5 | no |
| Student Checking | 30 | 5 | yes |
| Everyday Checking | 30 | 5 | yes |
| Interest Checking | 30 | 5 | yes |
| Premier Checking | 30 | 5 | yes |
| Private Client Checking | 30 | 5 | yes |

The new-account period is 30 calendar days and the hold is to the 5th business day after deposit on every tier. Access Checking is the one tier on which paper checks cannot be written, so it is a checkless account.

**Boundary illustration (hypothetical).** A check deposited to an Everyday Checking account on the 29th calendar day after opening falls inside the new-account period and posts on the 5th business day after deposit. A check deposited on the 31st calendar day falls outside it.
